Corporate.tagline: Branded podcasts, audio strategy, and production services.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Sterling is a real adjective meaning of high standard or genuine — historically referring to silver of certified quality. As a brand name it signals dependable trade quality without being literal about audio. Audio Group is the plain category structure that places the brand as a multi-service operator. The pair reads as an established mid-tier audio production house — the kind of vendor branded-podcast budgets actually go to (Pacific Content, Lower Street, JAR Audio).
Corporate.manifesto: Sterling Audio Group is a full-service audio production company providing branded podcast production, audio strategy, and end-to-end show development for corporate clients. The buyer is a head of brand, a CMO, or an internal communications lead. The contract is the year, often multi-year. The deliverable is a fully produced, distributed, measured podcast programme.
Corporate.industrySummary: Branded podcasting has matured into a recognized B2B service category dominated by a small number of specialist production agencies. The opening is for a serious mid-tier studio with strong narrative-production craft, measurable distribution outcomes, and the procurement-grade reliability enterprise marketing teams require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Pacific Content (pacific-content.com) is the branded-podcast reference. Lower Street (lowerstreet.co) holds the B2B branded peer slot. JAR Audio (jaraudio.com) sits in the production-services middle. Pineapple Street Studios (pineapple.fm) plays in the editorial-branded peer position. We belong with Pacific Content and Lower Street in the mid-tier branded-podcast category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Sterling Audio Group is a full-service branded podcast production company serving corporate clients with strategy, production, distribution, and measurement.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on narrative-production craft, distribution capability, and the operational reliability corporate clients require for sustained programmes.

Run RFPs for new agency relationships every two to three years.
Care about narrative quality and distribution reach equally.

Need measurable outcomes against published targets.
Need a partner who can sustain a multi-year programme.

Reference real client brands in case material.

Creative.tagline: A podcast network for the close-mic conversations.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Lavalier is the trade name for the small clip-on microphone used in intimate recording — single trade noun. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most podcasts are scared of having an opinion. They hedge, they centrist, they cite three sources before saying anything. The Lavalier Co is the network for shows whose hosts have something to say and aren't going to soften it for a sponsor.
Creative.industrySummary: Podcast brand has been cautious and clean. There's room for a network that's loud, opinionated, sticker-friendly, and still produces shows that hold up under criticism.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Barstool Sports (barstoolsports.com) has the loud-male side. The Ringer (theringer.com) holds the sports-culture middle. Crooked Media (crooked.com) does the political version. We sit somewhere between The Ringer and Pushkin in tone.
Creative.positioningStatement: A podcast network for shows that aren't afraid to be wrong on tape.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Has strong opinions about media, sports, technology, or culture. Listens to two or three shows weekly. Tells friends to listen. Wears the merch.

dos: Make jokes
Quote the worst lines from the hosts
Promote with real reactions from listeners
donts: Sand the edges off the hosts
Run sponsor reads that pretend to be content
Apologize for the shows we put out

Creative.tagline: Shows you'd overhear in a good bar.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Earshot is a real word for the distance within which a conversation can be heard — slightly literary, slightly intimate, immediately evocative of the eavesdropping pleasure good podcasts deliver. Podcast Co. is the plain category suffix. The pair reads as a small, warm production house with a clear point of view — closer in tone to Radiotopia or Pineapple Street than to a corporate network.
Creative.manifesto: Most podcast networks chase scale. More shows, more genres, more downloads. We started Earshot because the actually good podcasts feel like overhearing a great conversation in a bar — specific, unhurried, with a clear point of view from a host you start to like. The network is small. The shows are warm. The conversations stay specific.
Creative.industrySummary: Editorial podcast networks have proliferated. The opening is for a network with a tonal point of view — warm, conversational, slightly bar-room — that differentiates from both the polished prestige networks (Pushkin) and the genre-driven entertainment networks (Wondery).
Creative.competitorLandscape: Radiotopia (radiotopia.fm) holds the indie-editorial peer slot. Pineapple Street Studios (pineapple.fm) plays in the warm-editorial middle. Defector (defector.com) sits in the journalist-owned peer position. The Ringer (theringer.com) is the conversational-network reference. We sit alongside Radiotopia with a stronger tonal identity.
Creative.positioningStatement: Earshot Podcast Co. is a small editorial network producing warm, conversational shows with clear hosts and unhurried pacing.
Creative.positioningRationale: The network competes on tone. Every show on the roster is selected for warmth, specificity, and host personality — not for category fit or download projections.

Want unhurried pacing.
Want hosts they can imagine having a drink with.

Creative.tagline: A podcast network that records to tape.

Creative.mission: To produce podcasts in the heritage tape tradition.
Creative.vision: A network whose shows are archived on the same reels their producers used.
coreValues: Warm — tape is the medium.
Specific — every show is tape-recorded.
Considered — the reel is the craft.
Literary — the writing about tape is part of the work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Reel references the tape reel — the physical medium of analog audio. Audio is the plain category suffix. Direct compound, no 'The' prefix.
Creative.manifesto: Most podcast production is digital from microphone to file. We started Reel Audio because the actual best audio character comes from tape — saturated, warm, mastered from the reel.
Creative.industrySummary: Tape recording is mostly historical. There is real space for a creative-led network that uses tape as the primary medium.
Creative.competitorLandscape: The Tape Hiss Co (within the catalog, music) plays the closest analog peer. Most podcast networks are digital. We sit further out — podcasts recorded to tape.
Creative.positioningStatement: Reel Audio is a podcast network producing shows recorded to physical tape and mastered from the reel.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the tape premise.
